ai.title: Rename ignoreHelicone flag and refactor fine-tuning dataset scripts
ai.summary: Renamed `ignoreHelicone` to `ignoreDatabaseAndHelicone` in `backend/src/claude.ts` to accurately reflect that the flag bypasses both Helicone logging and database persistence. Moved fine-tuning dataset generation scripts to `scripts/patch-dataset-processing/` and exported `updatePatch` and `updateSketch` functions for modular reuse. Dataset entry interfaces now include `updatedPatch` and `updatedSketch` fields, and parallel processing count increased from 5 to 10.

eli5.text: The system now more accurately labels a setting that, when turned on, skips saving your conversation to the internal database and stops sending a copy of it to a third-party logging service for review; previously the name suggested only that logging was skipped, which was misleading. Behind the scenes, the team also reorganized the scripts that build training data for the assistant into one dedicated folder, made two of those scripts reusable by other parts of the system, and allowed more conversations to be processed at the same time. If you interact with it directly, nothing will look different right away, because these are internal improvements to how the system tracks and records your activity.

ai.title: Add web usage tracking page and move quota manager to common
ai.summary: New /usage page and /api/usage endpoint expose credit consumption via shared usageDataSchema. AnonymousQuotaManager.checkQuota now returns concrete Date instead of SQL<Date>, with creditsUsed and endDate resolved in DB query. Quota manager moved from backend/src/billing to common/src/billing to enable web API access.

eli5.text: You can now open a dedicated page in the app (called '/usage') to see how many of your monthly credits you've used and how many are left, and the same numbers are shown through the navigation bar as you move around. Behind the scenes, the part of the system that keeps track of credit limits was moved out of the server-only code into shared code that the web app can read directly, so it no longer has to fetch the numbers indirectly through a separate server request. Starting today, when you visit that usage page, the server asks the updated credit tracker for your current month-to-date usage and the date your credit counter resets, and it sends back exactly those four figures: credits used, total credits, remaining credits, and the next reset date. Anonymous visitors do not get this page.

ai.title: Updated favicons and added YouTube demo video
ai.summary: Replaced PNG favicon with ICO format and updated Apple touch icon in web/public/favicon/. Added embedded YouTube demo section to web/src/app/page.tsx. Navbar logo switched from lucide-react BrainCircuitIcon to local favicon image in web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx.

eli5.text: The website now shows a playable YouTube video of a demonstration right on the home page, so visitors can watch how the tool works without leaving the site. The small icon that appears in a browser tab has also been swapped to a different picture format, and the logo at the top of every page now uses that same updated icon image. Anyone opening the site in a browser will see the new video and the refreshed logo.

ai.title: generate-patch uses gpt-4o-2024-08-06 fine-tuned model
ai.summary: generate-patch model reference updated to `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` with `generate-patch-batch2` suffix and new fingerprint `AKYtDIhk`. Previous `gpt4o` constant replaced with explicit dated model string. Change scoped to `backend/src/generate-patch.ts`. Fine-tuned model variant switched to batch2.

eli5.text: The assistant that writes code patches now uses a newer, more capable version of its underlying system instead of the older one it was using before. You won't notice any change in how the patch generation works, but the system now references a fine-tuned model variant internally so the generated patches should be more consistent. This change is already live and only affects the internal tool that creates code suggestions.
